sections.h2: What is Clay County, Missouri, like for a property owner?
sections.html:
Clay County is the northern suburban side of the Kansas City area. Liberty is the county seat, and Kansas City is the largest city, with a portion of it inside the county. It was organized on January 2, 1822 and named for Henry Clay. At 397 square miles of land it is the fourth-smallest county in Missouri by area, yet the 2020 census made it the fifth most populous with 253,335 residents. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 265,032.

The neighbors are Clinton County to the north, Ray to the east, Jackson to the south, Platte to the west and Wyandotte County, Kansas to the southwest. Interstates 29, 35 and 435 cross the county, along with U.S. 69, 71 and 169. Other communities include Gladstone, North Kansas City, Excelsior Springs, Kearney, Smithville and Missouri City.

sections.h2: Where do I pay Clay County property tax and who do I call?
sections.html:
The Collector's site is claycountymo.tax, where residents search a bill, pay and set up prepayments. Two offices take walk-in business, both open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

  • Main office: Administration Building, 1 Courthouse Square, Liberty, MO 64068.
  • Clay County Annex: 1901 NE 48th Street, Kansas City, MO 64118.
  • Collector phone: 816-407-3200. Assessor phone: 816-407-3500.
  • County Clerk, who takes Board of Equalization forms: 816-407-3570, with Stacey Tingle as the clerk.

The 2026 payment deadline is posted as Wednesday, December 31, 2026. The county follows the state holiday calendar, and its list shows offices closing at noon on December 24 and staying closed December 25 and 26.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Clay County value?
sections.html:
The county's Board of Equalization page lays out the sequence. Contact the Assessor before you send any form to the Clerk's office. The board can lower a value that sits above true value compared with other properties, and it can also raise one it finds too low, so weigh that before filing.

StepWhenHow
Informal hearing with an Assessor's appraiserAprilCall the Assessor's office for an appointment
Board of Equalization applicationPostmarked or delivered by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in JulyForms go through the County Clerk
Board of Equalization hearingAugustRequests go through the Clerk's office
State Tax Commission appeal30 days after the board's final action or September 30, whichever is laterFile after the board decides

The July date matches RSMo 137.275, and the commission step follows RSMo 138.430.

sections.h2: What if a Clay County valuation jumped?
sections.html:
Missouri law shifts the burden in one situation. Under RSMo 138.060, when an assessed valuation rose at least 15 percent from the previous assessment, other than from new construction or improvement, the Assessor must prove the valuation does not exceed true market value. The statute also says no presumption exists that the Assessor's figure is correct.

  • Pull the prior and current notices and compare the percentage change.
  • Gather recent sales of similar houses near yours, plus repair estimates for defects the Assessor may not know about.
  • Book the April informal hearing, then decide whether to file with the board by the July deadline.

New residents should know that assessments follow where you lived and what you owned on January 1. The Assessor's office handles people arriving from another county or state, and the collector's site says to bring the previous county's personal property tax receipt to the DMV.

sections.h2: How does the Clay County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax ends up in an online auction run through GovEase. The 2026 calendar shows how the process runs, and every date in it has now passed. Fees of $135 were added to bills still delinquent on May 4, 2026, and $115 more on June 1. The last day to pay by card, personal check or online was June 14, 2026, after which properties headed to sale needed cash, cashier's check or money order. The sale itself opened at 10:00 a.m. on August 24, 2026.

  • Owners of land sold in 2025 had an absolute right to redeem until 5:00 p.m. on August 25, 2026, with funds received in person at the Liberty office. Postmarks and drop box payments did not count.
  • After that, redemption continues until an investor claims a deed.
  • Land that failed to sell after the third offering became available over the counter beginning the week of September 14, 2026.
  • Overbid money is held for the person legally entitled to it. Homeowners and recorded lienholders have 90 days after the deed is claimed to apply, and after 91 days it passes to the county school fund.

The page for the next sale shows no 2027 dates yet. Ask the Collector at 816-407-3200 for the schedule.

sections.h2: How do Clay County schools affect a home sale?
sections.html:
School districts serving the county include Liberty, North Kansas City, Kearney, Smithville, Excelsior Springs and Missouri City. Liberty has two high schools, Liberty and Liberty North. North Kansas City runs a larger system with North Kansas City, Oak Park, Staley and Winnetonka high schools.

The Metropolitan Community College district covers the Liberty and North Kansas City portions of the county as its in-district taxing area. William Jewell College, a private four-year school, is in Liberty. Because each district sets its own levy, two houses with the same assessed value can carry different bills, so confirm the district on the statement before you quote a tax figure to a buyer.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Clay County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau QuickFacts page for Clay County gives a picture of the market buyers are shopping in.

  • Housing units in 2025: 110,443, with 69.5 percent owner-occupied.
  • Median owner-occupied value, 2020 to 2024: $275,600.
  • Median gross rent: $1,243.
  • Median household income: $88,468.
  • Population density: 637.1 per square mile in 2020.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 297.
  • Mean travel time to work: 22.8 minutes.

About 91.9 percent of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census, and 8.1 percent in rural areas.

faqs.q: What is the Clay County, MO property tax due date for 2026?
faqs.a: Wednesday, December 31, 2026, according to the Collector's holiday and dates table. Offices are closed December 25 and 26 and open again after that. Pay at the Liberty courthouse, at the Annex on NE 48th Street in Kansas City, or through claycountymo.tax.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Clay County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 816-407-3500 and ask for an informal hearing, which is held in April with an appraiser. If that does not settle it, the County Clerk at 816-407-3570 handles Board of Equalization forms, and the board application is due by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July.

faqs.q: Can the Clay County Board of Equalization raise my value?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's board page says the board can lower a value that exceeds true value compared with other properties, and it can raise a value it finds too low. Weigh that before filing, and bring comparable sales that support your number.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County tax sale?
faqs.a: The 2026 sale was held online through GovEase starting at 10:00 a.m. on August 24, 2026, so it has passed. The 2027 date is not posted on the Collector's tax sale page. Call 816-407-3200 for the schedule, and for redemption or overbid questions.

faqs.q: Do I owe Clay County tax if I just moved here?
faqs.a: Assessment depends on where you lived and what you owned on January 1. A person who moved in from another Missouri county or from out of state should call the Assessor at 816-407-3500. Use the personal property tax receipt from the earlier county when you register a vehicle.
